title: improv·artist · computational (Vera Molnar)
mutation_directive: improv artist: computational via Vera Molnar

improv_extras.practice: algorithmic line drawings 1960s onward; deviation from the grid as expression

v1.feedback: Strong Molnar translation — the perturbation grid with rotating disorder gradient is a genuine algorithmic idea, not decoration. The parchment-on-midnight palette is restrained and correct. Two refinements: the orthographic camera with no pan/drift means the piece is entirely static in framing — adding a very slow lateral drift (0.001/frame) would give it a contemplative breathing without violating the no-autoRotate rule. The ghost-dot grid underneath is a nice touch but at opacity 0.13 it's nearly invisible on most monitors; bump to 0.18-0.22 so the tension between order and deviation actually reads.

v2.feedback: Faithful Molnar translation — perturbation gradient is immediately legible and the parchment-on-midnight palette is exactly right. The piece is essentially planar; giving the rectangles a slight z-displacement proportional to perturbation (even ±0.3) would reward orbiting and add sculptural depth without betraying the 2D source. The ghost crosshair layer is a nice conceptual touch but at gl_PointSize 3 and alpha 0.20 it may be invisible on many monitors — consider bumping to 0.30 or dropping it if it can't be read. The breathing animation could modulate perturbation amplitude (tight center pulses outward) rather than uniformly scaling all rects, so the viewer watches order dissolve and reconstitute — closer to Molnar's generative process.
